mainTopic: Liability for doing קרבן rites outside the עזרה: where it is learned from, how the חטאות are counted, where 'outside' begins, and whether it applies today.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about which קרבן rites make a person liable when done outside the בית המקדש. The גמרא shows that you cannot learn this liability from what two rites share (צד השוה), because the תורה wrote a separate פסוק for זריקה. רבי אבהו then counts how many חטאות a person brings for doing several rites outside, according to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. אביי disagrees, saying the פסוק ״שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה... שָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״ sets the count for everyone. A ברייתא uses the words 'in the camp' and 'outside the camp' to mark the exact line: slaughtering outside the עזרה is punished, while slaughtering in the wrong spot inside it, like an עולה in the south, is not. עולא and רבא then argue about slaughtering on the roof of the היכל. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether offering outside is punished today, which depends on whether the first holiness of the מקדש lasts forever. They argue again about whether a bone attached to the meat counts toward a כזית. The amud ends as רבא begins a new question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggestion: learn it from what the two cases share
steps.stepSummary: Each single comparison failed, so the גמרא suggests learning liability from the common feature of both cases together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be derived from what the two cases have in common.
steps.whatsHappening: Each single comparison was knocked down, so the גמרא tries a new method: learn the liability from what both earlier cases share. This sets up the next move, where the idea is tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone had its own special feature that blocked the comparison. Using both together gets around that, because the feature that blocks one source is missing in the other. This is the method of צד השוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it come; let it be derived
From between them; from what the two cases share
The common feature of two sources, used to learn a law

phrases.english: Let it be derived from between them.
phrases.notes: Literally 'from between them.' It means learning from what the two earlier cases have in common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the earlier refutations of each single comparison by combining both sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that there is no source for liability for the rite under discussion done outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each single source was refuted by a different special feature, so a צד השוה of both should still work and make him liable.

steps.title: If so, the verse about sprinkling would be unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the צד השוה method: if it worked, the תורה would not need to write a פסוק about זריקה outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the תורה should not have mentioned sprinkling. Let it be derived from what the other two share!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion by pointing to זריקה. If learning from a common feature worked, the תורה would not need a separate פסוק for זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by looking at what the תורה actually did. The תורה did write a פסוק for זריקה. If זריקה could have been learned from a צד השוה, that פסוק would be extra, so the method must not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that were true
Let it not be said; the verse would be unnecessary
Sprinkling the blood of a קרבן on the מזבח

phrases.english: If so, let it not be stated regarding sprinkling,
and let it be derived from between them!
phrases.notes: Here 'them' means שחיטה and העלאה, which the next line spells out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the צד השוה suggestion of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire method of learning liability for rites done outside from a צד השוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the פסוק about זריקה outside unnecessary.

steps.title: Working out how sprinkling could have been derived
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that זריקה can't be learned from שחיטה alone or from העלאה alone, but could be learned from what they share.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you try to learn sprinkling from slaughtering, you can object: slaughtering is special, because a פסח becomes invalid if slaughtered for people who can't eat it. If you try to learn it from offering up, you can object: offering up is special, because it applies to a מנחה too. But you could still learn it from what the two share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא walks through the derivation to prove the point in step 2. Each source alone fails, but together they would work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה has a special strictness: in a פסח it becomes invalid when done שלא לשם אוכלין. העלאה has its own special strictness: it applies even to a מנחה. Neither strictness is found in both sources, so a צד השוה would teach זריקה, and the פסוק would be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
Offering up parts on the מזבח
For the sake of people who cannot eat it
The Passover offering
Meal offering

phrases.english: And if you derive it from slaughtering –
what about slaughtering? It is special, since it becomes disqualified
when done for the sake of those who cannot eat, in the Paschal offering;
phrases.notes: Slaughtering the פסח for people who can't eat it ruins the קרבן. Sprinkling the blood that way does not.

phrases.english: derive it from offering up –
what about offering up? It is special, since it applies to a meal offering;
but let it be derived from between them;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out step 2's claim that זריקה could have been learned from a צד השוה.
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק about זריקה would be unnecessary if צד השוה worked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The separate refutations of שחיטה and העלאה, which a combined צד השוה would overcome.

steps.title: The verse was written to block learning from the common element
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote the פסוק about זריקה precisely to teach that liability for rites done outside is not learned from a צד השוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the verse was written: to tell you that this cannot be derived from what two cases share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the extra פסוק about זריקה is there to teach a rule: you can't learn this kind of liability from a צד השוה. So the suggestion in step 1 fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of being a wasted פסוק, it becomes a teaching tool. Since even זריקה needed its own פסוק, no other rite done outside can be made liable through a צד השוה. Each liability needs a direct פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason
A verse is written
That it does not come; it cannot be derived

steps.whatToRemember: Liability for doing a קרבן rite outside cannot be learned from a צד השוה. The פסוק about זריקה proves it, so a rite with no פסוק of its own stays exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes off the last way to make someone liable for a rite done outside without a direct פסוק.

phrases.english: For this reason the verse is written,
to say that it is not derived from between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the תורה wrote a פסוק for זריקה even though it could have been learned, and uses this to reject step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liability for rites done outside needs a direct פסוק. A צד השוה is not enough, so the rite under discussion is not liable.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: Slaughtering and sprinkling outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו rules that a person who did both שחיטה and זריקה outside brings one חטאת according to רבי ישמעאל and two according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: if someone slaughtered and sprinkled outside, רבי ישמעאל says he is liable once, and רבי עקיבא says he is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו shows a practical difference that comes out of the earlier argument about where זריקה outside is learned from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל learns זריקה from the פסוק about שחיטה, so the two count as one prohibition and he is liable once. רבי עקיבא learns זריקה from the פסוק about העלאה, so שחיטה and זריקה are separate prohibitions and he is liable twice.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered the animal
He sprinkled the blood
According to the view of
Liable once, meaning he brings one חטאת

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an argument that looks only like a question of where a law is learned from can change how many קרבנות a person has to bring.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
One who slaughtered and sprinkled (outside),
according to Rabbi Yishmael, is liable once;
according to Rabbi Akiva, he is liable twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a practical result on top of the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא about the source for זריקה outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שחיטה plus זריקה outside: one חטאת according to רבי ישמעאל, two according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: אביי: Even רבי עקיבא says only once
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that even רבי עקיבא would say only one חטאת, because the פסוק ״שָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״ groups all the services into one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even רבי עקיבא holds he is liable only once, because the verse says "there you shall do," and the verse made all of them one service.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבי אבהו's count for רבי עקיבא's view and brings a פסוק to support his own count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says ״שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה״ for העלאה, then ״שָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״ for everything else. So all the other services, including שחיטה and זריקה, count as one service. The count therefore does not depend on where זריקה is learned from.

keyTerms.meaning: "There you shall do" (דברים 12:14)
The פסוק
One single service
He is liable only for

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not denying that זריקה outside is forbidden. He only says it is grouped with שחיטה as one service when we count the חטאות.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even according to Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: he is liable only once,
as the verse says: "There you shall do" —
phrases.notes: דברים 12:14. Earlier in that פסוק it already said "there you shall offer up."

phrases.english: the verse made all of them one service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אבהו's count for רבי עקיבא in the case of שחיטה plus זריקה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אבהו's claim that רבי עקיבא counts two in the case of שחיטה plus זריקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The count is set by ״שָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״, which groups all the non-העלאה services together, and not by the source of זריקה.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: Sprinkling and offering up outside
steps.stepSummary: Continuing his statement, רבי אבהו rules that for זריקה plus העלאה outside, רבי ישמעאל counts two and רבי עקיבא counts only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sprinkled and offered up outside, רבי ישמעאל says he is liable twice, and רבי עקיבא says he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a second case, which is the mirror image of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, זריקה belongs with שחיטה, so it is separate from העלאה and he is liable twice. For רבי עקיבא, זריקה is learned from the העלאה passage, so the two count as one and he is liable once.

keyTerms.meaning: He offered up the קרבן on an altar
Liable twice, meaning he brings two חטאות

phrases.english: One who sprinkled and offered up (outside),
according to Rabbi Yishmael, is liable twice;

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Akiva, he is liable only once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case from רבי אבהו, the mirror image of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זריקה plus העלאה outside: two חטאות according to רבי ישמעאל, one according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: אביי: Even רבי עקיבא says twice
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that even רבי עקיבא would say two חטאות, because the פסוק deliberately separates ״שָׁם תַּעֲלֶה״ from ״שָׁם תַּעֲשֶׂה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even רבי עקיבא holds he is liable twice, because that is why the verse split them: "there you shall offer up" and "there you shall do."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי again rejects רבי אבהו's count for רבי עקיבא, this time using the same פסוק in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists העלאה on its own and all other services together, so העלאה is always a separate prohibition. Anyone who does זריקה and העלאה is liable twice. For אביי, the same פסוק decides both cases for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: For this reason
Separated them
"There you shall offer up" (דברים 12:14)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אבהו counts the חטאות based on where זריקה is learned from: one for רבי ישמעאל and two for רבי עקיבא in שחיטה plus זריקה, and the opposite for זריקה plus העלאה. אביי says the פסוק sets the count for everyone: העלאה is separate, and all other services count as one.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even according to Rabbi Akiva, he is liable twice;
for this reason the verse separated them:
"There you shall offer up" and "there you shall do."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אבהו's count for רבי עקיבא in the case of זריקה plus העלאה, using the same פסוק as step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אבהו's claim that רבי עקיבא counts only one in the case of זריקה plus העלאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק separates העלאה from all other services, so they are always two prohibitions, no matter where זריקה is learned from.

steps.title: Doing all three services outside: everyone says two
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו finishes his statement: someone who did שחיטה, זריקה and העלאה outside brings two חטאות according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered, sprinkled the blood and burned the offering, all outside, everyone agrees he owes two חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds the last case of his statement: what happens when a person did all three services outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, שחיטה and זריקה count as one, and העלאה counts on its own, so that makes two. According to רבי עקיבא, שחיטה counts on its own, and זריקה and העלאה count as one, so that also makes two. The groups are split up differently, but both sides end up with the same total.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone; all opinions agree
He burned the offering (העלאה, putting it up on a מזבח)
He must bring two חטאות

steps.whatToRemember: The rabbis disagree about which services are joined together. Even so, for all three services done together, both sides end up at two חטאות.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think two means 'one for each pair'. Each side joins together a different pair of services, and both totals simply come out to two.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered, sprinkled, and burned (all outside) –
according to everyone he is liable for two.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁחַט וְזָרַק וְהֶעֱלָה לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי אבהו's statement by putting together his two earlier rulings (steps 5 and 7).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing שחיטה, זריקה and העלאה outside makes a person owe two חטאות according to both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: A ברייתא: slaughtering an עולה in the south is not punished
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the words 'in the camp' might make us think that slaughtering an עולה in the south of the עזרה is punished. The words 'outside the camp' show that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: 'In the camp'. You might think that someone who slaughters an עולה in the south side should be liable. So the פסוק says: 'outside the camp'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads ויקרא 17:3 closely. It starts with a guess that is wrong and then fixes it from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is supposed to be slaughtered in the north part of the עזרה. Because of the word 'in the camp', we might think that even slaughtering it in the south counts as the forbidden act. The second phrase, 'outside the camp', shows the punishment is only for slaughtering outside the עזרה altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: Camp; here it means an area around the משכן or the מקדש
Burnt offering, which must be slaughtered in the north of the עזרה
You might have thought; this brings up a wrong guess
So the פסוק says; this brings the verse that settles the question

phrases.english: The rabbis taught: 'In the camp' –

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל הַשּׁוֹחֵט עוֹלָה בַּדָּרוֹם יְהֵא חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: you might think one who slaughters an עולה in the south should be liable?
phrases.notes: An עולה belongs in the north side of the courtyard, so the south is the 'wrong spot', but it is still inside.

phrases.english: So the verse says: 'outside the camp'.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בַּמַּחֲנֶה״ – יָכוֹל הַשּׁוֹחֵט עוֹלָה בַּדָּרוֹם יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a ברייתא about where slaughtering counts as 'outside'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering an עולה in the south of the עזרה does not bring the punishment for slaughtering outside.

steps.title: Is someone only liable outside all three camps?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now asks the opposite question: maybe a person is liable only if he slaughters outside all three camps? It shows from the word 'in the camp' that he is liable even inside the לויה camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he is liable only outside all three camps. (So the פסוק says, 'or goat, in the camp'.) How do we know he is liable even in the camp of the לויים? So the פסוק says: 'in the camp'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא checks the other side. If 'outside the camp' were the only words, maybe nothing would count until you are outside everything. The word 'in the camp' answers that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were three areas, one inside the other: the camp of the שכינה (the עזרה), the camp of the לויים, and the camp of ישראל. 'Outside the camp' alone might mean outside all three. The phrase 'in the camp' shows you are liable even inside the outer camps, as long as you are outside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The three camps: שכינה, לויה, and ישראל
The camp of the לויים, the middle area around the משכן
From where do we know?

phrases.english: You might think he is liable only outside all three camps?
(So the verse says: 'or goat, in the camp'.)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: From where do we know he is liable even in the camp of the לויים?
So the verse says: 'in the camp'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the other extreme after step 10: if 'outside the camp' is the guide, maybe you must be outside everything.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a person liable only outside all three camps, or also inside the outer camps?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'in the camp' shows that he is liable even inside the לויה camp.

steps.title: Both phrases together set the exact line
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא comes back to the first worry: if we only had 'in the camp', the south might count. 'Or outside the camp' balances it, so the line is exactly the edge of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק said only 'in the camp', you might think that one who slaughters an עולה in the south is liable. So the פסוק says: 'or outside the camp'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by showing why both phrases are needed. Each one stops the other from being stretched too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the camp' by itself would reach too far inward, all the way to the south of the עזרה. 'Outside the camp' by itself would reach too far outward, to beyond all three camps. Together they set the line: slaughtering anywhere outside the עזרה is punished, and a wrong spot inside the עזרה is not.

keyTerms.meaning: If; here, 'if we only had this word'
The camp of the שכינה, the inner area (the עזרה)
North, the proper place to slaughter an עולה

steps.whatToRemember: The punishment for slaughtering outside depends on the edge of the עזרה. Inside it, even in the wrong spot, he is not liable. Outside it, even inside the outer camps, he is liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common ברייתא pattern: two parts of one פסוק each hold the other back, and together they mark one exact line.

phrases.english: If it said only 'in the camp',

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל הַשּׁוֹחֵט עוֹלָה בַּדָּרוֹם יְהֵא חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: you might think one who slaughters an עולה in the south should be liable?
So the verse says: 'or outside the camp'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בַּמַּחֲנֶה, יָכוֹל הַשּׁוֹחֵט עוֹלָה בַּדָּרוֹם יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 used 'in the camp', this step shows that reading needs the second phrase to hold it back, which brings the ברייתא full circle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both phrases are needed. Liability starts right outside the עזרה, and a wrong spot inside the עזרה does not make a person liable.

steps.title: Why the south of the courtyard does not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its reasoning: 'in the camp' is compared to 'outside the camp', so it only counts a place unfit for every קרבן. The south of the עזרה is fit for קדשים קלים, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'outside the camp' is a place unfit for slaughtering any קרבן, light or most holy, so 'in the camp' means a place like that. This leaves out the south of the עזרה. It is unfit for קדשי קדשים, but it is fit for קדשים קלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the conclusion it began in step 12. It explains exactly why slaughtering in the south of the עזרה is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words of the פסוק teach each other. 'Outside the camp' sets the pattern: a place where no קרבן at all may be slaughtered. 'In the camp' is limited to places that fit that pattern, and the south does not fit, because קדשים קלים may be slaughtered there.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... is special. A way of learning one case from the special feature of another.
The most holy קרבנות (like an עולה), which must be slaughtered in the north.
קרבנות of lighter holiness, which may be slaughtered anywhere in the עזרה.
The south side of the עזרה.

steps.whatToRemember: A place only counts as 'in the camp' for שחיטת חוץ if no קרבן at all may be slaughtered there. The south of the עזרה is fit for קדשים קלים, so slaughtering there is not punished.

phrases.english: Just as 'outside the camp' is special
phrases.notes: Both 'in the camp' and 'outside the camp' come from the same פסוק, ויקרא 17:3.

phrases.english: in that it is not fit for slaughtering holy offerings
or for slaughtering any offering at all;
this leaves out the south,
because even though it is not fit
for slaughtering the most holy offerings,
it is fit for slaughtering offerings of lighter holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא's conclusion from step 12 by giving the exact reason for the line.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'In the camp' only covers places unfit for every קרבן, so the south of the עזרה is not included.

steps.title: עולא: slaughtering on the roof of the Sanctuary makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: עולא uses the ברייתא's rule: the roof of the היכל is not fit for any קרבן, so slaughtering there makes a person חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Someone who slaughters a קרבן on the roof of the היכל is חייב, because that spot is not fit for slaughtering any קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא applies the rule just learned to a new case: the roof of the היכל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the test is whether a place is fit for any קרבן at all. The roof of the היכל is fit for none, so by that test it counts like 'outside', even though it sits within the holy area.

keyTerms.meaning: The roof of the היכל, the main Temple building.
Liable, here meaning punished for שחיטת חוץ.
Since; it gives the reason.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: הַשּׁוֹחֵט עַל גַּגּוֹ שֶׁל הֵיכָל – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: One who slaughters on the roof of the Sanctuary is liable,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין רָאוּי לִשְׁחִיטַת כׇּל זֶבַח.
phrases.english: since it is not fit for slaughtering any offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's test from step 13 for a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering on the roof of the היכל makes one חייב for שחיטת חוץ.

steps.title: רבא: the words 'entrance of the Tent of Meeting' exclude the roof
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if the only test were 'fit for no קרבן', the פסוק would only need 'outside the camp'. The extra words 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד' must come to exclude the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged this: If so, the פסוק could have written only 'outside the camp', without needing 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד'. Why do I need 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד'? Isn't it to exclude the roof?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks עולא's ruling with an argument from extra words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the פסוק also requires that the animal was not brought 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד'. Since the היכל matches the אהל מועד, someone on its roof did bring the animal there. So those words seem to exclude the roof, against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, a strong objection.
If so; it brings out a problem in what was just said.
Why do I need it? It asks what an extra word is for.
To exclude a case.
The entrance of the אהל מועד, the place a קרבן must be brought to.

phrases.english: Rava challenged it:
If so, let the verse write
'outside the camp',
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: and it would not need 'to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting';
Why do I need 'to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting'?
Is it not to exclude its roof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that slaughtering on the roof of the היכל makes one חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra words 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד' would add nothing unless they exclude the roof, which counts as being at the אהל מועד.

steps.title: The same question turned against רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks רבא the same kind of question: then the פסוק should only say 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד'. Why does it also need 'in the camp' and 'outside the camp'? Isn't it to include the roof?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא: If so, let the פסוק write only 'to the entrance of the אהל מועד'. Why do I need 'in the camp' and 'outside the camp'? Isn't it to include the roof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבא's own style of argument back against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'entrance of the אהל מועד' were the only test, the camp words would be extra. 'Outside the camp' is needed to exclude the south, so 'in the camp' still seems extra. It must teach that some place inside the holy area is punished, and the roof fits, just as עולא said.

keyTerms.meaning: To include a case.
In the camp, a word from ויקרא 17:3.

phrases.english: And according to Rava, if so, let it write:
'to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting';
why do I need 'in the camp' and 'outside the camp'?
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: Is it not to include its roof?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same method as רבא's challenge in step 15 against רבא himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the roof is excluded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On רבא's reading, the words 'in the camp' seem to have no job unless they include the roof.

steps.title: רב מרי: 'in the camp' covers an animal with its neck outside
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי defends רבא: 'in the camp' comes to include an animal whose body is inside the עזרה while its neck is outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: It comes to include a case where the whole animal is inside, but its neck is outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the question on רבא by finding a different job for the words 'in the camp'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words do not need to include the roof. They teach that even when most of the animal stands inside the עזרה, slaughtering a neck that is outside is still punished. So רבא can still say the roof is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it inside, meaning the animal's body is in the עזרה.
Its neck outside, where the actual cut happens.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
It is to include where all of it is inside
and its neck is outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra words a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In the camp' seemed to have no job unless it included the roof of the היכל.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In the camp' includes an animal whose body is inside the עזרה while its neck is outside, so רבא can still exclude the roof.

steps.title: Neck outside is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מרי's case: if the neck is outside, of course he is חייב, since the slaughter happens outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If its neck is outside, that is obvious! What does the תורה care about? The slaughter. And here the slaughter is outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב מרי's answer from step 17. It says we do not need a פסוק to teach his case, because the answer is obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה cares about where the שחיטה happens. The cut is made at the neck. If the neck is outside the עזרה, the slaughter is outside, so of course he is חייב. A פסוק would not be 'used up' on something this obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why would we need a source for it?
The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') is particular about this
Its neck, where the שחיטה cut is made

phrases.english: Its neck outside — that is obvious!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. It points back to רב מרי's case of body inside, neck outside.

phrases.english: About what is the Merciful One particular? About the slaughter;
and the slaughter is outside!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case רב מרי gave in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מרי's claim that 'in the camp' includes an animal with its body inside and its neck outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The place of the שחיטה is what counts, and the cut is at the neck. So a neck outside is obviously slaughtering outside, and no פסוק is needed to teach it.

steps.title: Body outside, neck inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns רב מרי's case around: 'in the camp' includes an animal whose whole body is outside but whose neck is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to include an animal whose whole body is outside but whose neck is inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב מרי's answer by flipping the case, so the פסוק now teaches something that is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the neck, where the cut is made, is inside the עזרה. You might think that makes it an inside שחיטה, so he is פטור. The extra words 'in the camp' teach that he is still חייב. This keeps רבא's reading in place: the roof is excluded, and 'in the camp' has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in another case
Its whole body is outside
Inside the עזרה

steps.whatToRemember: 'In the camp' includes an animal whose body is outside even though its neck is inside. This lets רבא keep using 'the entrance of the אהל מועד' to exclude the roof.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to include
its whole body outside but its neck inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by changing the case to one that is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case (reversing which part is inside and which is outside)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the neck, where the cut is made, is inside, you might think he is not חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is חייב, because the animal's body is outside. 'In the camp' teaches this, so רבא's reading stands.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's reading stands. 'In the camp' includes the body-outside, neck-inside case, and the roof is excluded.

steps.title: Offering outside today: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute: someone who offers a קרבן outside in our times. רבי יוחנן says he is חייב; ריש לקיש says he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: someone who offers up a קרבן outside nowadays. רבי יוחנן says he is liable; ריש לקיש says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings an argument between two אמוראים about offering a קרבן outside when there is no בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin of offering outside (העלאה בחוץ) usually means offering outside when you could offer inside. Today there is no בית המקדש, so the question is whether this sin still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers up a קרבן on an altar
In our times, when there is no בית המקדש
Liable / exempt

phrases.english: It was stated: one who offers up nowadays —
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: he is liable,
Reish Lakish says: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The earlier discussion about 'in the camp' is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: offering outside today makes one חייב. ריש לקיש: one is פטור.

steps.title: Does the first holiness last forever?
steps.stepSummary: The reason behind each view: רבי יוחנן holds the first holiness of the מקדש lasts forever; ריש לקיש holds it was only for its own time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because the first holiness made the place holy for its time and also for the future. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because the first holiness made it holy for its time but not for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא rules the way he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place is still holy, a person could offer there even today. Offering outside is then a real sin, so רבי יוחנן says חייב. If the holiness ended when the מקדש was destroyed, there is no proper place to offer now, so ריש לקיש says פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The first holiness given to the place of the מקדש
For its own time, while the מקדש stood
For the future, even after it is destroyed

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on one question: is the place of the מקדש still holy today?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says he is liable —
the first holiness sanctified it for its time
and sanctified it for the future to come.
Reish Lakish says he is exempt —
the first holiness sanctified it for its time
but did not sanctify it for the future to come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר חַיָּיב – קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the two rulings in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the first holiness lasts forever, so he is חייב. ריש לקיש: it was only for its time, so he is פטור.

steps.title: Is this an older argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are just repeating the argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that they disagree about the same point that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argued about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that this argument may already appear among the תנאים. It is setting up a source to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא often checks whether a dispute between אמוראים matches an earlier one between תנאים. If it does, each אמורא is simply following one תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion
A dispute
They disagree

phrases.english: Shall we say that in the dispute
of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא דְּבִפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to tie the dispute in step 21 to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש match the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע?

steps.title: Curtains while building the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה: רבי אליעזר says that while the second מקדש was being built, they put up curtains in the היכל and the עזרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר said, when they were building the היכל, they made curtains for the היכל and curtains for the courtyards. But in the היכל they built from outside, and in the courtyard they built from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that holds the older argument, starting with רבי אליעזר's view. This sets up the comparison, and רבי יהושע's view comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the walls were being rebuilt, they hung temporary curtains to mark off the holy areas. The builders worked from outside the curtains in the היכל and from inside them in the עזרה. The גמרא will use this to ask whether the holiness depended on the place having walls or partitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Curtains, used here as temporary walls
The main building of the מקדש
The courtyards of the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This quote is not finished here. רבי יהושע's part of the משנה comes next, and only then can you see how it compares to רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Eliezer said:
When they were building the Sanctuary —
they would make curtains for the Sanctuary,
curtains for the courtyards;
except that in the Sanctuary they built from outside,
and in the courtyard they built from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה that step 22 referred to, starting with רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש matches the one between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in עדיות: רבי אליעזר's report about curtains put up while the second מקדש was being built.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the first holiness lasts forever
steps.stepSummary: The quote from the משנה continues. רבי יהושע says that offerings could be brought, and holy foods eaten, even without a building, curtains, or a wall, because the first holiness lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I heard that they brought offerings even when there was no מקדש building. They ate קדשי קדשים even without curtains, and קדשים קלים and מעשר שני even without a city wall. This is because the first holiness made the place holy for its own time and also for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה it started in the last step. Now we hear רבי יהושע's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע lists three levels of holiness: the מזבח, the עזרה, and ירושלים. Each one stays holy even when its physical boundary is missing. His reason uses the exact words רבי יוחנן used: the first holiness lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: The מקדש building itself
The most holy offerings, eaten only inside the עזרה
Offerings of lesser holiness, eaten anywhere in ירושלים
Second tithe produce, eaten in ירושלים
The wall around ירושלים
For the future, meaning forever

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: I heard

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ מַקְרִיבִין אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בַּיִת,
phrases.english: that they would offer sacrifices even though there was no Temple building,
and they would eat the most holy offerings
even though there were no curtains,
and offerings of lesser holiness and second tithe
even though there was no wall;
because the first holiness made it holy for its time
and made it holy for the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quote begun in Step 23, giving רבי יהושע's opinion.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are repeating the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עדיות: רבי יהושע explicitly says the first holiness lasts forever

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר must hold the holiness ended
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that since רבי יהושע needed the 'lasts forever' reason, רבי אליעזר must hold that the holiness did not last. That would make the two disputes the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't this show that רבי אליעזר holds that the first holiness did not last forever?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the משנה. It seems to answer the question from Step 22: yes, it is the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר spoke of putting up curtains, which suggests the place needed new boundaries to be holy again. רבי יהושע said none was needed because the holiness lasts. So רבי יוחנן would match רבי יהושע, and ריש לקיש would match רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it follow that... (drawing an inference)
Holds, is of the opinion

phrases.english: Does it not follow that Rabbi Eliezer
holds that it did not make it holy forever?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר לֹא קִידְּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש repeating the argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It seems so: רבי אליעזר holds the holiness ended, matching ריש לקיש.

steps.title: רבינא: maybe they both agree
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the inference. Maybe both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that the holiness lasts forever, and each one simply reported a different thing he heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: How do you know that? Maybe everyone agrees that the first holiness was for its own time and also forever. One Sage told what he heard, and the other Sage told what he heard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back on the conclusion from the last step. He says the משנה does not prove that the two תנאים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר only described what they did, putting up curtains. He never said the holiness had ended. So the two reports can fit together, and the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש may be new.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
Perhaps
Everyone agrees
What he heard (from his teachers)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבינא as saying רבי אליעזר holds the holiness ended. His whole point is that both תנאים may agree it lasts forever.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מִמַּאי?
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: From where do you know this?
Perhaps everyone agrees
that the first holiness made it holy for its time
and made it holy for the future;
and one Sage said what he heard,
phrases.notes: The first 'Sage' here is רבי אליעזר, and the second one is רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: and the other Sage said what he heard!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in Step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds the first holiness did not last
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה shows two different reports, not a disagreement. Both תנאים may hold that the holiness lasts forever.

steps.title: Then why did רבי אליעזר need curtains?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא, still speaking, anticipates a problem with his own reading. If רבי אליעזר also holds the holiness lasts, why were curtains needed at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: According to רבי אליעזר, why were curtains needed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא himself brings up a likely objection to his reading (וְכִי תֵּימָא is still part of his words to רב אשי). The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place stayed holy without any walls, curtains would seem pointless. The fact that רבי אליעזר mentions them suggests he thought they were needed to make the place holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (bringing up a possible objection)
Why do I need it?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: קְלָעִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: And if you will say: According to Rabbi Eliezer, why do I need curtains?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: קְלָעִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a problem with רבינא's claim from Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that רבי אליעזר agrees the first holiness lasts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the place was already holy, curtains would serve no purpose. So mentioning them suggests they were needed for holiness.

steps.title: The curtains were only for privacy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the curtains were only for privacy, not to create holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were just for privacy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection from the last step. The curtains had a practical reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curtains were not needed to make the place holy. They gave the holy service some privacy. So רבי אליעזר can still hold that the holiness lasts, and רבינא's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Privacy, modesty
Merely, only

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע may both hold that the first holiness lasts forever. So the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש does not have to copy theirs.

phrases.english: Merely for privacy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised in Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of a detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The curtains were needed to make the place holy, so רבי אליעזר holds the holiness ended.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curtains were only for privacy, so רבי אליעזר can agree the holiness lasts.

steps.title: New dispute: bone completing an olive-size
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: someone offers outside a piece with less than a כזית of meat, but the bone brings it up to a כזית. רבי יוחנן says he is חייב; ריש לקיש says he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If someone offers something up outside that does not have a כזית of meat, but the bone completes it to a כזית, רבי יוחנן says he is חייב, and ריש לקיש says he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand new topic. It is another argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about offering outside the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being חייב for offering outside requires a piece the size of a כזית. The question is whether bone counts toward that size. רבי יוחנן counts it, and ריש לקיש does not.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers up (here, outside the מקדש)
The size of an olive, the minimum amount
Bone
Completes it, makes up the missing amount

phrases.english: It was said: One who offers up, and there is not an olive-size in it,
but the bone completes it to an olive-size
Rabbi Yochanan says: he is liable,
Reish Lakish says: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the first holiness ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If bone completes a כזית offered outside, רבי יוחנן holds he is חייב and ריש לקיש holds he is פטור.

steps.title: The reason behind each side: does an attached bone count?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he is חייב because something attached to a part that goes up on the מזבח is treated like that part. ריש לקיש says he is פטור because an attached item is not treated that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he is liable, because things attached to what goes up on the altar count like what goes up. ריש לקיש says he is exempt, because things attached to what goes up do not count like what goes up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the dispute from the last step and now gives the reason behind each opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bone on its own does not need to go up on the מזבח. רבי יוחנן says that while it is still attached to the meat, it counts as part of the meat, so it fills out the כזית and the person is חייב. ריש לקיש says the bone stays separate in the eyes of the law, so there is less than a כזית and he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Things attached to parts that go up on the מזבח, like a bone attached to the meat
They are treated like the parts that go up
Liable, punishable for offering outside
Exempt, not liable

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument turns on one idea, חיבורי עולין. רבי יוחנן says an attached item counts like the part that goes up. ריש לקיש says it does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Both agree that a loose bone by itself does not count. They only argue about a bone that is still attached to the meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains the dispute and becomes the basis for further questions about attached items.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: he is liable,
things attached to what goes up are like what goes up.
phrases.notes: Here that means the bone attached to the meat counts as part of the meat that goes on the מזבח.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: he is exempt,
things attached to what goes up are not like what goes up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר חַיָּיב – חִיבּוּרֵי עוֹלִין כְּעוֹלִין דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the dispute stated in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an attached bone counts as part of the meat, so he is חייב. ריש לקיש: it does not count, so he is פטור.

steps.title: רבא begins a new question
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to ask a question about someone who offers something up outside. The rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if someone offers up...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רבא opens a new question about a person who offers something outside, and the details come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעי tells us this is an open question, not a challenge. Since it comes right after the dispute about attached items, it likely builds on that discussion, but we have to wait for the rest of the case.
